collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A researcher counts with knots, and a weaver's patterns already count: work together, or keep separate.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has invented a way of keeping count with knots on cords: one knot for each basket of fish. (friend), who weaves, looks at it and laughs: (friend.his/her) patterns have always counted things, the rows and repeats and turns. Neither of them knew. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) and (friend) work together all season, and come up with a cord that can count fish, days, and people in a single string. The village uses it to keep the stores. Nobody else understands it. (subject) and (friend) find this hilarious.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: Each keeps their own way. (subject)'s cords keep count of the stores. (friend)'s patterns keep count of the family stories. Years later, a young researcher finds both and works out that they say the same things.
